# Implementation Plan: Fasting Goal Timer

**Branch**: `020-fasting-goal-timer` | **Date**: October 28, 2025 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/020-fasting-goal-timer/spec.md`

**Note**: This document was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command. See `.specify/templates/commands/plan.md` for the execution workflow.

## Summary

Add goal-setting and progress tracking capabilities to the existing live fasting timer (Feature 017). Users can set a target fasting duration via preset buttons (12h, 16h, 18h, 24h) or custom input, view real-time progress with percentage-based bar visualization, and see calculated goal completion time. Goals are session-based (stored in React Context + localStorage) and persisted to the Entry model only when the fast ends. This enables future analytics on goal completion rates and willpower tracking.

**Technical Approach**: Extend Entry model with optional fields (fastingGoal, goalStatus), create React Context for session state management with localStorage fallback, build progress calculation in useMemo hook synced with 60-second timer updates, implement inline collapsible goal-setting UI with validation, and modify POST /api/entries endpoint to accept goal data.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: JavaScript (ES6+) with React 19.1.0, Next.js 15.5.6 (App Router)  
**Primary Dependencies**: Next.js, React, Mongoose 8.19.1, date-fns 4.1.0, Tailwind CSS, lucide-react  
**Storage**: MongoDB with Mongoose ODM (extends Entry model with 2 optional fields)  
**Testing**: Jest + React Testing Library (unit/integration), Playwright (E2E)  
**Target Platform**: Web (responsive, mobile-first), supports modern browsers  
**Project Type**: Web application (Next.js App Router with API routes)  
**Performance Goals**: <10s goal setting, <1s progress updates, <1% timestamp calculation error, 100% data persistence  
**Constraints**: 60-second update frequency (matches existing timer), session-based storage (no DB writes during fast), 1-168 hour goal range  
**Scale/Scope**: Single-feature enhancement, ~6 new components, 2 model fields, 1 modified API endpoint, zero breaking changes

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### ✅ I. Next.js Best Practices
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: Using App Router (Next.js 15.5.6), Client Components for interactive UI (goal setting, progress display), Server Components where possible, following file-based routing conventions
- **Evidence**: React Context for state management, client-side interactivity marked with 'use client' directive, API routes for backend logic

### ✅ II. Mobile-First Responsive Design  
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: Inline collapsible panel (not modal) for mobile-first UX, preset buttons in 2x2 grid with 44px+ touch targets, responsive progress bar, number input with `inputmode="decimal"` for mobile keyboard
- **Evidence**: Research decision R-006 documents mobile-first approach, touch-friendly button sizes specified

### ✅ III. Test-Driven Development (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- **Status**: PASS  
- **Implementation**: Tests will be written before implementation (TDD cycle). 23 acceptance scenarios in spec provide test cases. Unit tests for validation, integration tests for API, component tests for UI, E2E tests for critical flows.
- **Evidence**: Spec has testable acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then format, quickstart includes testing checklist, 8 measurable success criteria

### ✅ IV. Component Architecture
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: Atomic design followed - GoalSettingPanel (molecule), GoalProgressDisplay (molecule), FastingTimer (organism). Components are self-contained, reusable, independently testable. Props documented with JSDoc.
- **Evidence**: Quickstart shows clear component hierarchy, separation of concerns (Context for state, hooks for logic, components for presentation)

### ✅ V. User Privacy & Data Security
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: Goal data is user-specific health tracking, protected by existing NextAuth authentication. API endpoint requires authenticated session. No PII in goal data. localStorage used only for session persistence (non-sensitive).
- **Evidence**: API contract specifies authentication required, goal data tied to userId, same security model as existing entry data

### ✅ VI. Performance & Accessibility
- **Status**: PASS
- **Implementation**: Progress bar includes ARIA attributes (role="progressbar", aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax). Semantic HTML throughout. Keyboard navigation supported. Performance targets: <10s goal setting, <1s updates, <1% calculation error.
- **Evidence**: Success criteria SC-001 through SC-008 define measurable performance targets. Progress bar component includes ARIA attributes. Research validates <1ms calculation time.

7. **R-007: Goal Data Persistence Timing** - Decided: Write on fast completion (POST /api/entries)
8. **R-008: Input Validation Rules** - Decided: 1-168 hours, decimals, validate on blur

## Risk Mitigation

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| **localStorage quota exceeded** | Fallback to Context-only (lose on refresh) |
| **Browser refresh loses goal** | Document in UX, acceptable per spec |
| **Timezone edge cases** | Acknowledged in spec, client-side acceptable |
| **>100% progress confusion** | Clear UI: green bar + checkmark + "exceeded" text |
| **Validation bypass** | Duplicate validation in API (server-side) |
| **Entry model breaking change** | Optional fields ensure 100% backward compat |
